name: Field Doctor-Style Coq au Vin (Low FODMAP)
ingredients:
260 g Chicken
260 g Sliced Potatoes
3 medium Carrots
240 g Oyster Mushrooms
160 g Extra Virgin Olive Oil
55 g Spinach
55 g Celeriac (CELERY)
46 g Tomato Puree [tomato]
46 g Red Wine [Water, Red Wine, Salt, SULPHITES]
1/4 medium Swedes
15 g Fennel
15 g Peas
1 1/2 tsp Tamari [water, SOYA beans, sea salt]
2 tbsp Parsley Flat
1/2 tsp Tapioca Starch
1/3 tsp Lemon Zest
pinch of Chicken Stock (Chicken Extract, Chicken Fat, Salt], Herb Mix, Brown Sugar, Sea Salt, Black Pepper
directions:
1. Potatoes: Roast or boil sliced potatoes until tender; keep warm.

2. Brown chicken: Season chicken and brown well in olive oil; set aside.

3. Vegetables: In the same pan, cook carrot, oyster mushrooms, celeriac, swede and fennel until coloured.

4. Braise: Stir in tomato puree, red wine, chicken stock, tamari, brown sugar, herb mix, lemon zest, salt and pepper. Return chicken, cover and simmer (or oven 170°C) until chicken is cooked and sauce is glossy — thicken with tapioca slurry if needed.

5. Finish: Wilt spinach; scatter parsley. Serve chicken and sauce with the potatoes and peas stirred through or on the side.
 
Cool, portion into 8, refrigerate up to 3 days or freeze; reheat until piping hot.
description:
Ingredients: Water, Chicken, Sliced Potatoes, Carrot, Oyster Mushrooms, Extra Virgin Olive Oil, Spinach, Celeriac (CELERY)...

Home recreation inspired by Field Doctor Coq au Vin (Low FODMAP) (~355 g ready meal). Scaled to 8 portions. Not an official Field Doctor recipe. https://www.fielddoctor.co.uk/products/coq-au-vin
notes:
REVERSE-ENGINEERED from Field Doctor published ingredients for personal home cooking only. Official meal is Monash Low FODMAP certified at single-serve size.

Scaling notes
Scaled for 8 portions from Field Doctor single serve (~355 g x 8 = 2840 g).
Unlabelled amounts inferred from UK descending-weight ingredient order (each item <= the one above and >= the one below; leftover mass shared on that basis, not equally).
Spoon measures use ingredient density (g per tsp) then round to kitchen fractions.
Amounts above 50 g are rounded to the nearest 5 g for cooking convenience.
Sweet peppers ~140 g each; carrots ~80 g; sweet potatoes ~130 g; courgettes ~175 g; aubergines ~250 g; swedes ~800 g; plum tomatoes = 400 g tins; lemon ~45 ml / lime ~30 ml juice.
Duplicate label ingredients merged (higher amount kept).
Liquid for home cooking: cook rice, quinoa, pasta, noodles and potatoes in water as you normally would (salt the water; drain where appropriate). For sauces, braises and stir-fry glazes, add water or stock gradually until the consistency is right — do not try to measure the ready-meal's residual water.
Low FODMAP: no onion or garlic bulbs — use chives / green tops only. Inspired recreation from Field Doctor ingredients, not an official recipe.
Chives listed in grams to match fresh packs (e.g. Waitrose Cooks' Ingredients Chives, 20 g).
Ready-meal residual water was ~259 g (inferred ~9.12% from list order) and is not listed as an ingredient.
Extra Virgin Olive Oil is kept as an ingredient on this recipe because the ready meal is relatively oil-rich (or pesto-style); still fry/roast in extra virgin olive oil as directed.
